source.title: Learning a Generative Meta-Model of LLM Activations
source.authors: Grace Luo; Jiahai Feng; T. Darrell; A. Radford; Jacob Steinhardt

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses a scaling-law form and the FLOPs estimate C = 6ND, following Kaplan et al., but its measured loss is GLP activation-diffusion loss, not held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The paper reports scaling results for a generative model of LLM activations and for that model's steering and probing utility. These are related analogues, not measurements of the claim's language-model pretraining loss, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or downstream language-model performance.
record.test_reason: The study fits a power law to the loss frontier of flow-matching diffusion models trained on LLM activations. The fit spans about 1e15–1e19 FLOPs and four model sizes (0.5B–3.3B). This is a new modality and objective, so R1 bears on V5: whether the same power-law form holds beyond text pretraining. The study does not measure language-model pretraining loss, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation or architecture shape. The reader's T4 label understates this, because the scaling result is the study's own measured finding, not a tool.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that GLP diffusion loss falls as a smooth power law in compute, halving the gap to its floor per ~60x compute. They also conclude that steering and probing utility track the loss, so diffusion loss is a reliable proxy for downstream utility. They further claim that continued scaling should yield further gains, but they do not test this.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a flow-matching diffusion objective on LLM activations and fits GLP loss against compute; it does not measure language-model held-out cross-entropy or sweep parameter/token allocation. It follows Kaplan et al. for the FLOPs estimate and power-law approach.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports cleaner probing scaling trends for noisier GLP inputs (t = 0.5 rather than t = 0.1) and averages steering scaling results over relative coefficients r ≥ 1, where GLP is most helpful.

fits_no_version.finding: GLP steering quality (concept and fluency mean, r≥1) and 1-D probe AUC rise with GLP compute, following fitted power laws in compute. They are roughly linear in diffusion loss (Figs. 2b, 2c, 11, 15). Dense probing shows a similar trend (Fig. 14).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For activation diffusion models, downstream interpretability utility (steering, probing) improves predictably with model compute and tracks diffusion loss.

record.problems: The results do not measure the claim's held-out language-model cross-entropy. The loss curve is GLP training diffusion loss, and the scaling sweep uses 0.5B–3.3B GLPs trained for one epoch on 1B activations. The paper does not validate small-run extrapolation to much larger runs or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. The steering and probing scaling figures do not state uncertainty intervals.

untested.parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss varied over parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fit validated against much larger runs. The authors only suggest continued scaling will help.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation sweep; data is fixed at 1B activations.
No depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count. Width is fixed at 2x the activation dimension, and the authors only say sufficient width is critical.
Other training regimes (repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer) and image/video models not tested. Only one new modality (LLM activations), one source model (Llama1B) and one layer.
No language-model downstream tasks as a function of LM scale or loss.
No comparison of fitting methods or parameter-counting choices. Only one fit form, applied to the envelope.

missing.what: Multi-layer GLP loss-vs-compute curve compared with the single-layer curve. Figure 9 gives the iso-loss FLOPs exchange rate (multi-layer needs more compute). This bears on whether the power-law form holds across training setups.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source. The scaling result is in a non-language-model setting (diffusion over LLM activations), so it bears only on V5 as a new modality. The fit is to a loss envelope from four sizes with no confidence intervals, and the loss reported is training loss from a single epoch.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy while varying language-model parameters, tokens, or compute.
Does not test whether power laws fitted on small language-model pretraining runs predict much larger runs.
Does not vary language-model parameter and token allocation under fixed compute or estimate a compute-optimal split.
Does not compare language-model depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
Does not test whether language-model pretraining loss laws transfer across modalities or the listed training regimes; GLP diffusion loss is a different objective and system.
Does not test downstream language-model task performance as a function of language-model scale or pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitting or setup choices for language-model pretraining scaling laws or compute-optimal allocation.

rows.subject: GLP (Generative Latent Prior)
rows.stage_stated: activation diffusion model trained on Llama1B activations
rows.operation_detail: Fits a power law to the compute-efficient frontier of GLP diffusion training loss.
rows.measure: GLP diffusion training loss as a function of compute
rows.note: The fitted result aggregates the compute-efficient frontier across the reported GLP size sweep; it is not a held-out language-model cross-entropy result.
rows.check: Should link to V5. The diffusion loss follows a fitted L(C)=0.52+435.1·C^-0.169 envelope over about four decades of compute (Fig. 2a). Caveats: it is training loss, though single-epoch, so close to held-out; it comes from only four model sizes; no uncertainty is given on the fit.

rows.subject: GLP (Generative Latent Prior)
rows.stage_stated: activation diffusion model trained on Llama1B activations
rows.operation_detail: Measures positive-sentiment steering performance across GLP compute scales.
rows.measure: Concept & Fluency Mean as a function of compute
rows.note: Aggregate scaling result across GLP checkpoints; the text says steering performance improves with compute.
rows.check: Steering utility of the GLP vs compute is a downstream metric of a non-LM activation model. It does not measure what V6 names (downstream performance of language models with scale or pretraining loss). It is averaged only over coefficients r≥1, where checkpoint spread is largest. It belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: GLP (Generative Latent Prior)
rows.stage_stated: activation diffusion model trained on Llama1B activations
rows.operation_detail: Measures 1-D probing performance across GLP compute scales.
rows.measure: Average 1D Probe AUC as a function of compute
rows.note: Aggregate scaling result across GLP checkpoints; the text says probing accuracy improves with compute and reports no plateau in the plotted curves.
rows.check: 1-D probe AUC vs GLP compute is a downstream utility of an activation model, not LM downstream performance. The t=0.5 timestep was chosen as giving the cleanest trend. It belongs in fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: Unconditional flow-matching MLP diffusion models (0.5B–3.3B) trained one epoch on 1B Llama1B middle-layer FineWeb activations; ~1e15–1e19 FLOPs
relationships.reason: R1: the training-loss envelope fits a power law plus irreducible term (E=0.52, α=0.169) smoothly across the compute range, from only four model sizes.
relationships.display_finding: The training-loss envelope fitted an offset power law with E=0.52 and α=0.169 across the compute range, using four model sizes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
